the problem of transforming a range scan into a 3D structured mesh representation.
the problem of converting an unstructured range scan into a 3D CAD-like mesh representation.
the generation of 3D mesh models from unstructured 3D point clouds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper introduces Scan2Mesh, which is a neural network that can generate a 3d mesh from an unstructured range scan of a real world object.
we present a novel neural architecture which generates 3D mesh representations from range scans.
this paper presents an approach that generates meshes from point clouds, and that the generated meshes are more detailed and accurate than those produced by other methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the first data driven approach that transforms an unstructured 3D scan into a structured mesh, a key step towards creating a generative 3D mesh pipeline for 3D modeling applications.
we are able to generate 3D meshes with a single forward pass on the input scan, which can be further processed by downstream applications.
Scan2Mesh can take an input range scan of an object, and generate a structured mesh representation of the same object.
The main takeaway from our work is that
generative models can be used to produce structured 3D representations of 3D objects, which can be used as an input to downstream applications.
the generation of a mesh representation of a 3d object is a fundamentally different problem from the generation of an implicit function representation.
a generative model can be trained on a small dataset of range scans to produce a mesh that can be further refined and used for downstream tasks such as 3D printing, animation, and CAD modeling.
